config.description: The loss fix alone: globally-pooled weighted Pearson with a running statistic, everything else exactly as v011.
config.hypothesis:
The single most important fix in this repo's history, and it was sitting in plain sight. This repo trained nineteen versions on a loss whose own docstring lied: chunk_loss() accepted a `state` argument and claimed it 'carries the moments across chunks so the statistic is cumulative rather than restarted'. The body never read `state`, and the call site never passed it. The weighted-Pearson statistic was therefore recomputed from each chunk's own rows and restarted 20 times per sequence.

That is exactly the failure dozken/wunder documents and calls out by name: a per-chunk Pearson subtracts a weighted mean estimated from that chunk alone, so the slow level component the metric actually scores is discarded and any per-chunk level offset is free. Their chunk4k runs 'win within-sequence correlation and lose on level drift', and models trained on their chunk loss get WORSE with more training (0.575 -> 0.553) instead of better. Their fix -- a running detached sufficient statistic pooled over the batch as well as over time -- is the 2026-09-15 metric, which pools every scored row of every sequence into ONE correlation per target.

Expected: a large gain, larger than anything else we have tried, because every prior run was optimising a surrogate that structurally cannot see the quantity being scored. Our +0.058 over the organiser baseline came from the soft mask and the state reset on top of a mis-specified loss; with the loss correct those two should compound rather than merely survive.
config.change_vs_parent:
ONE change off gru_v011: the loss. chunk_loss now keeps a running detached sufficient statistic [sum w, sum wy, sum wp, sum wy^2, sum wp^2, sum wyp] pooled over BOTH the batch and the time axis into one value per target, reset every stats_window steps (default one sequence's worth of chunks). The previous implementation recomputed the statistic from each chunk's own rows and discarded it, despite accepting a `state` argument it never read.
Unchanged: the soft mask, state_reset 4000, chunk_len 2000, aux weighted-MSE 0.05, EMA 0.999, architecture 2x128 proj0 (192,258 params), seed 1337, 3-epoch cosine schedule, data (train shard only).

train_time_metrics.aggregation: mean of two target-wise global clipped Weighted Pearson correlations over all masked rows

score_interpretation: Clean held-out score: 0.678374, trained on train alone. This is a REGRESSION against its parent v011 (0.679986), -0.001613, which is 5.1x the 0.000317 noise floor. v019 tested replacing the per-chunk Pearson loss with a globally-pooled running-statistic loss, changing nothing else. The loss fix as implemented here does not help and is clearly harmful. Shipped for completeness and to document the result; not a promotion candidate.
recommendation: Do not submit. v011/v017 are strictly better.
